reuse.why: Extends the existing getDateWithSkippedWeekend and reuses recurConfigToRSchedule/dayFromDate, but the daily-skip rule is not put in a shared helper so getDatesInRange re-implements it.

duplication.why: The weekend-or-holiday predicate is defined twice (inside getNextDate and inside getDateWithSkippedWeekend), and the daily-skip condition is written once in getNextDate and again in getDatesInRange.

placement.why: Holiday matching and adjustment sit in shared/schedules.ts as expected, but the daily-skip rule lives inside getNextDate's body and is re-expressed in the server handler instead of in the shared date-adjustment definition.

scope.why: Edits are confined to schedule date logic, the new handler, the RecurConfig type and tests; the minor variable rename in getNextDate is incidental.

maintainability.why: A future change to the skip rule must be made in getNextDate's loop, getDatesInRange's inline check and getDateWithSkippedWeekend, and getUpcomingDates/schedule-template silently do not apply the daily rule at all.

bypasses_abstraction.where: schedules/app.ts getDatesInRange checks frequency==='daily' && skipWeekend && (isWeekend||isHoliday) itself instead of going through the shared rule in shared/schedules.ts getNextDate.

disguised_duplication.where: isSkippedDay closure in getNextDate vs isSkippedDay in getDateWithSkippedWeekend (same weekend||holiday test, reshaped); daily-skip condition reshaped as a .map returning null in getDatesInRange vs a search loop in getNextDate.

abstraction_drift.where: getDateWithSkippedWeekend gains skipWeekend and holidays parameters; getNextDate gains a daily-frequency special-case branch with its own search loop; getDatesInRange re-implements the daily skip check rather than calling a shared definition.
